source.quote: a Hookean or linear elastic regime for ε<60% with a stable tangent modulus (dσ/dε) of ~30 kPa … The maximum σ was 10.6 kPa for the first elastic regime and 36.1 kPa at 80% strain … The maximum shear σ of the FIBER NFAs was 8.82 kPa with a large yield shear ε of 61%.

records.notes: Cylinders ~28 mm diameter, 3% prestrain, strain rate 30 mm/min. Same sample also measured in shear (sandwich clamp, 4 mm thick, to 100% shear strain): elastic to ~40% shear strain, plateau 40-70%, max shear stress 8.82 kPa, yield shear strain 61%; shear tangent modulus is plotted (Fig. 2f) but no number is printed. Tension (Fig. 2h): Young's modulus 62 kPa, max yield value 4.33 kPa, brittle. Alternate numbers for the same 9.60 mg/cm3 sample in SI Table 1: E' = 40.3 kPa, "Max stress" = 32.4 kPa (columns not defined in the SI; likely a dynamic storage modulus and a max stress at an unstated strain). gaps: Gross & Fricke, Nanostructured Materials 6, 905 (1995), 'Scaling of elastic properties in highly porous nanostructured aerogels' (DOI verified in Crossref): closed access, no abstract in any API; not opened. The only source for the silica E ~ rho^3.6 here is the Burger/Emmerling/Fricke/Weth 1997 review.
Woignier & Phalippou 1989: only the abstract was obtained (exponents 3.7/2.6/1.6); density range and prefactors not obtained. Full text on HAL/EDP is behind bot protection.
Ma, Roberts, Prevost, Jullien, Scherer 2000: abstract only (E ~ rho^3.6 from DLCA finite-element simulations, theory not measurement); no table or figure data.

Silica aerogel: no measured compressive strength at any density below 20 kg/m3, and no measured E on a monolith other than the order-of-magnitude 10^4 Pa at 5 kg/m3 (review, acoustic). Kucheyev et al. 2012 (Adv. Mater. 24, 776) abstract only: relative density <0.5% shows effective fracture strain >50%; no E or strength values.
Silica of about 1 kg/m3: no primary source opened. Burger et al. cites 3 kg/m3 (Tillotson & Hrubesh 1992, not opened); Si et al. 2014 intro gives '>1 mg/cm3' as a secondary statement.

Shear modulus: none measured for any aerogel below 10 kg/m3. Si et al. 2014 measured shear stress-strain at 9.6 mg/cm3 (max shear stress 8.82 kPa, yield shear strain 61%) but prints no shear modulus; Wu 2015 gives only the isotropic relation G = Y/2 for nu = 0 (model); Burger 1997 says shear modulus scales with density but gives no numbers; silica Poisson ratio ~0.22 (review).

Sun/Xu/Gao 2013 (0.16 mg/cm3), Hu 2013 (3 mg/cm3), Zou 2010 (4 mg/cm3), Gui 2010 (5-25 mg/cm3), Mecklenburg 2012, Worsley 2009 and 2012: paywalled; abstract-level densities only, no modulus or strength from a primary source. Aerographite compression moduli (1 kPa at 0.2 mg/cm3; 7 kPa at 15 mg/cm3) are from Wikipedia, unverified against the paper.
Gui et al., Adv. Mater. 22, 617 (2010) 'Carbon nanotube sponges': OpenAlex abstract contains no density or modulus values.

Worsley et al. CNT foams and graphene aerogels: no open full text found for APL 94, 073115 (2009) or Chem. Commun. 48, 8428 (2012); the Chem. Commun. abstract gives E ~ 50 MPa with no density. Open Shin et al. 2012 and a Baumann/Worsley note are at 28-300 mg/cm3 (above the family range).

Nanocellulose aerogels: no measured compressive modulus or strength found below 20 kg/m3. Sivaraman et al. 2022 (Carbohydr. Polym. 292, 119675) abstract: E ~ rho^1.53, E up to ~1 MPa, compression range 9-115 mg/cm3; abstract only.

Boron nitride: Xu 2019 modulus 25 kPa at 5 mg/cm3 and 'ultimate stress up to 0.14 MPa' (density/strain for the stress not stated); the SI with modulus vs density was not obtained. Lei 2015 BN aerogels (1.4-20 mg/cm3) report no mechanical values.

Most carbon/graphene 'strengths' available are stress at 80% strain (Qiu) or a 'Max stress' of undefined strain (Si SI Table 1), not yield or collapse strengths. Wu 2015 compressive stress values appear only in figures and were not extracted. Qiu does not define its compressive modulus extraction.
Zhu 2015 graphene microlattice moduli exist only in Fig. 5d (not extracted); densities mostly above 20 kg/m3.

Not opened: Nature 2022 'Hypocrystalline ceramic aerogels', Sci. Adv. 2019 cryogenic graphene elasticity (bot-blocked), Worsley JACS/graphene-CNT aerogels, Bryning SWNT aerogels, Kobayashi/Saito/Isogai nanocellulose aerogels.
